root.label: UK Income Tax
root.source: HMRC Annual Tax Summary methodology — https://www.gov.uk/government/collections/annual-tax-summary. Figures shown are on a FY 2022-23 basis and should be re-baselined against the latest published year before relying on specific percentages.
root.note: Income tax revenue allocated by central government across major spending categories. Excludes National Insurance, which is in principle hypothecated to contributory benefits and the NHS but in practice goes into the Consolidated Fund.

children.label: Welfare
children.source: DWP / HMT Public Expenditure Statistical Analyses
children.note: Working-age benefits, family support, housing assistance, disability and incapacity payments. State pension is shown as a separate line.

children.label: Working-age benefits (Universal Credit etc.)
children.source: DWP Benefit Expenditure and Caseload Tables 2023-24 (https://www.gov.uk/government/collections/benefit-expenditure-tables); allocation within the Welfare category of HMRC's Annual Tax Summary.
children.note: Universal Credit replaces six legacy benefits and supports people both in and out of work. The single largest item within working-age welfare.

children.label: Disability & incapacity benefits
children.source: DWP Benefit Expenditure and Caseload Tables — PIP, DLA, ESA and Attendance Allowance lines; HMRC Annual Tax Summary methodology.
children.note: Includes Personal Independence Payment (PIP), Disability Living Allowance (DLA, including child DLA), Employment & Support Allowance (ESA) and Attendance Allowance. Funds extra costs of daily living and mobility.

children.label: Child & family benefits
children.source: HMRC Child Benefit Statistics; DWP residual tax credit caseload data; HMRC Annual Tax Summary Welfare sub-allocation.
children.note: Child Benefit and residual tax credit payments. Tapered for higher earners via the High Income Child Benefit Charge.

children.label: Housing benefit (legacy)
children.source: DWP Housing Benefit Caseload Statistics; being absorbed into Universal Credit. Residual caseload is largely pensioners and supported-housing tenants.
children.note: Being absorbed into Universal Credit. Remaining caseload is largely pensioners and supported-housing tenants.

children.label: Administration
children.source: DWP Annual Report and Accounts — operating cost lines; allocation within HMRC Annual Tax Summary Welfare category.
children.note: DWP staff, IT systems, fraud and error operations, debt management.

children.label: Health
children.source: DHSC / NHS England annual report and accounts
children.note: Predominantly NHS England, with smaller allocations to social care, public health, research and arms-length bodies.

children.label: NHS front-line services
children.source: DHSC Annual Report and Accounts 2023-24; NHS England Annual Report. Front-line services include hospitals, primary care, community care, ambulance and mental health.
children.note: Hospitals, GP services, community and district nursing, ambulance, mental health, prescribing.

children.label: Adult social care (central contribution)
children.source: DHSC Annual Report — Better Care Fund and adult social care grant lines. Most adult social care is funded by local authorities via council tax and the social care precept; this is the central top-up only.
children.note: Most adult social care is funded by local authorities through council tax and the social care precept; this is the central government top-up via the Better Care Fund and grants.

children.label: Public health
children.source: Office for Health Improvement and Disparities (OHID, formerly Public Health England) reporting; UK Health Security Agency annual report.
children.note: Vaccination and screening programmes, health protection, smoking cessation, sexual health, drug and alcohol services.

children.label: Medical research & training
children.source: NIHR (National Institute for Health and Care Research) annual report; Health Education England (now part of NHS England) workforce-training reporting.
children.note: NIHR research funding, Health Education England, junior doctor and nurse training contributions.

children.label: NHS administration & arms-length bodies
children.source: DHSC ALB annual reports (NICE, CQC); NHS England HQ administration costs as published in NHS England annual report.
children.note: NHS England HQ, NICE, CQC, regulatory and commissioning support costs.

children.label: State pensions
children.source: DWP — single largest line item in welfare; reported separately in the HMRC summary

children.label: Education
children.source: DfE annual report
children.note: State schools, sixth forms and FE colleges, higher education teaching grant, early years and childcare entitlements. Excludes student loan outlay, which is accounted for separately.

children.label: National debt interest
children.source: DMO / OBR Economic and Fiscal Outlook
children.note: Coupon and indexation payments on UK gilts. Has risen sharply since 2022 due to higher interest rates and RPI uplifts on index-linked gilts.

children.label: Defence
children.source: MoD annual report
children.note: Armed forces pay and pensions, equipment procurement, intelligence services (SIS, Security Service, GCHQ), NATO contribution.

children.label: Public order & safety
children.source: Home Office, Ministry of Justice
children.note: Police forces, prisons and probation, courts and tribunals, fire and rescue, border force, immigration enforcement.

children.label: Transport
children.source: Department for Transport
children.note: Rail subsidy and Network Rail, strategic road network (National Highways), HS2, local transport grants, aviation and maritime regulation.

children.label: Business & industry
children.source: DBT, DESNZ
children.note: R&D tax relief offsets, energy support schemes, regional growth funds, trade promotion, post-office and shipbuilding subsidies.

children.label: Government administration
children.source: Cabinet Office, HMT
children.note: Running costs of central departments and cross-government functions not allocated to a specific service.

children.label: Culture, sport & heritage
children.source: DCMS
children.note: Arts Council England, museums and galleries, Sport England, heritage bodies, BBC World Service grant.

children.label: Environment
children.source: Defra, DESNZ
children.note: Flood defence, agricultural transition payments, environmental protection, waste, air quality.

children.label: Housing & utilities
children.source: DLUHC (now MHCLG)
children.note: Affordable housing programme, building safety remediation, regulation of water and energy networks (central share).

children.label: Overseas aid
children.source: FCDO
children.note: Cut from 0.7% to 0.5% of GNI in 2021 as a temporary measure. Includes humanitarian, development and multilateral commitments.

children.label: Other / rounding
children.source: Reconciliation residual — HMRC Annual Tax Summary published category percentages don't sum to exactly 100% due to rounding and small unallocated items (transitional EU payments, minor lines). Treated here as a single 'Other' bucket so the tree totals correctly.
children.note: Unallocated remainder. Reflects rounding in the published figures and minor items not assigned to a major category.

trees.label: British Gas
trees.prompt: If your annual gas bill was

root.label: British Gas — annual gas bill
root.source: Ofgem default tariff cap cost breakdown (https://www.ofgem.gov.uk/energy-policy-and-regulation/policy-and-regulatory-programmes/energy-price-cap); supplier-margin branch from Centrica plc Annual Report 2023 (https://www.centrica.com/investors/results-reports-presentations/). Top-level Ofgem percentages are firm; supplier-margin sub-allocations are illustrative — Centrica reports group-level figures, not per-customer-margin allocation.
root.note: British Gas is the retail brand of Centrica plc. The shape of every domestic gas bill in Great Britain is set by Ofgem's default tariff cap, which is built from a stack of cost components. Below is an approximate split of where each pound goes.

children.label: Wholesale gas
children.source: Ofgem default tariff cap; ICIS / Heren wholesale price benchmarks
children.note: The cost of buying the gas itself on the wholesale market. Suppliers hedge purchases months ahead, so the price you pay reflects past traded prices rather than the spot price on the day.

children.label: Norwegian pipeline gas
children.source: DESNZ Digest of UK Energy Statistics (DUKES) Table 4.3 — UK natural-gas imports by country of origin (https://www.gov.uk/government/statistics/digest-of-uk-energy-statistics-dukes). Norway has been the UK's single largest gas source since 2022.
children.note: Imported through the Langeled and Vesterled pipelines from the Norwegian Continental Shelf. Equinor (majority Norwegian state-owned) is the dominant supplier. Norway has been the UK's largest single source of gas since the loss of Russian supply in 2022.

children.label: UK Continental Shelf
children.source: DESNZ DUKES Table 4.1 — UK natural-gas production; North Sea Transition Authority (NSTA) field-level production data (https://www.nstauthority.co.uk/data-centre/data-downloads-and-publications/).
children.note: Domestic gas produced from North Sea and Irish Sea fields. Operators include Shell, BP, Harbour Energy, Spirit Energy and TotalEnergies. UK production is in long-term decline as fields mature.

children.label: LNG imports
children.source: DESNZ DUKES Table 4.3 (LNG imports by source country); National Gas Transmission entry-point flow data. Qatar and the US are the largest sources via Milford Haven (South Hook, Dragon LNG) and Isle of Grain terminals.
children.note: Liquefied gas shipped to terminals at Milford Haven (South Hook, Dragon LNG) and Isle of Grain. Major sources include Qatar (QatarEnergy) and the United States (Cheniere). LNG's share has grown sharply since 2022.

children.label: Storage, balancing & trading
children.source: National Gas Transmission system operator monthly reports; Ofgem Wholesale Markets Indicators quarterly. Covers National Balancing Point trading, line-pack management and storage charges.
children.note: Costs of using gas storage (Centrica's own Rough field reopened in 2022), and the National Balancing Point market mechanism that keeps the system in equilibrium.

children.label: Network costs
children.source: Ofgem RIIO-2 price control; National Gas / GDN regulated revenues
children.note: The cost of moving gas across the country and into your home. These charges are the same whoever your supplier is, because every supplier uses the same physical network.

children.label: Gas transmission
children.source: Ofgem RIIO-T2 final determinations for National Gas Transmission (price control period 2021-2026); sold by National Grid plc to a Macquarie-led consortium in early 2024 for ~£2.2bn equity. https://www.ofgem.gov.uk/energy-policy-and-regulation/policy-and-regulatory-programmes/network-price-controls-2021-2026-riio-2
children.note: Operated by National Gas Transmission, which carries gas at high pressure across Great Britain. Sold by National Grid plc to a Macquarie-led consortium in early 2024.

children.label: Gas distribution
children.source: Ofgem RIIO-GD2 final determinations (2021-2026) for the four UK gas distribution networks: Cadent (largest), Northern Gas Networks, SGN, and Wales & West Utilities. Allowed revenues published per GDN annual report.
children.note: Eight regional gas distribution networks deliver gas to homes at lower pressure. Cadent is the largest (covering much of England); the others are Northern Gas Networks, SGN and Wales & West Utilities. All are privately owned and regulated by Ofgem.

children.label: Metering & smart meter rollout
children.source: DESNZ Smart Metering Implementation Programme annual reports (https://www.gov.uk/government/collections/smart-meters-statistics); Ofgem price-cap methodology smart-meter net-cost component.
children.note: Costs of installing, maintaining and reading gas meters, including the national smart meter programme.

children.label: Operating costs
children.source: Ofgem operating cost allowance; Centrica annual report cost lines
children.note: The cost of running British Gas as a retail supplier: paying staff, engineers, billing systems, vans and IT. Also covers bad debt (customers who don't pay), which has risen materially since 2022.

children.label: Staff & field operations
children.source: Illustrative breakdown of the Ofgem default-tariff-cap operating-cost allowance. The cap sets a total operating allowance per customer; the split between staff, IT, bad debt, marketing and property is the supplier's internal allocation and is not directly disclosed in this form. Numbers triangulate from Centrica plc annual report cost lines plus the Ofgem allowance methodology.
children.note: Call centre staff, smart-meter installers, service engineers, account managers. British Gas employs around 20,000 people across the UK.

children.label: Billing, IT & customer systems
children.source: Illustrative breakdown of the Ofgem default-tariff-cap operating-cost allowance. The cap sets a total operating allowance per customer; the split between staff, IT, bad debt, marketing and property is the supplier's internal allocation and is not directly disclosed in this form. Numbers triangulate from Centrica plc annual report cost lines plus the Ofgem allowance methodology.
children.note: The infrastructure that produces your bill, runs the website and app, handles direct debits and meter reads.

children.label: Bad debt provisions
children.source: Illustrative breakdown of the Ofgem default-tariff-cap operating-cost allowance. The cap sets a total operating allowance per customer; the split between staff, IT, bad debt, marketing and property is the supplier's internal allocation and is not directly disclosed in this form. Numbers triangulate from Centrica plc annual report cost lines plus the Ofgem allowance methodology.
children.note: An allowance for customers who fall behind on their bills. The cap explicitly includes a bad-debt allowance which has been increased since the cost-of-living crisis began.

children.label: Marketing & customer acquisition
children.source: Illustrative breakdown of the Ofgem default-tariff-cap operating-cost allowance. The cap sets a total operating allowance per customer; the split between staff, IT, bad debt, marketing and property is the supplier's internal allocation and is not directly disclosed in this form. Numbers triangulate from Centrica plc annual report cost lines plus the Ofgem allowance methodology.
children.note: Advertising and switching incentives. Has fallen significantly since the price cap reduced the headroom for competition.

children.label: Property & overheads
children.source: Illustrative breakdown of the Ofgem default-tariff-cap operating-cost allowance. The cap sets a total operating allowance per customer; the split between staff, IT, bad debt, marketing and property is the supplier's internal allocation and is not directly disclosed in this form. Numbers triangulate from Centrica plc annual report cost lines plus the Ofgem allowance methodology.
children.note: Offices, call-centre buildings, depots, head-office functions.

children.label: Policy & social costs
children.source: BEIS / DESNZ levy schemes; Ofgem policy cost component
children.note: Government schemes funded through your bill rather than through general taxation. Smaller for gas than electricity; most green levies sit on the electricity bill.

children.label: Energy Company Obligation (ECO4)
children.source: DESNZ ECO4 Order 2022 (Statutory Instrument 2022/875); Ofgem ECO administration annual reports (https://www.ofgem.gov.uk/environmental-and-social-schemes/energy-company-obligation-eco). Largest single component of energy-bill policy costs.
children.note: Suppliers are required to fund insulation, heating upgrades and other efficiency measures for low-income and vulnerable households. The cost is recovered across all customer bills.

children.label: Warm Home Discount
children.source: DESNZ Warm Home Discount Regulations 2022 (SI 2022/687). £150 rebate per eligible household over winter, recovered from suppliers and spread across all bill-payers.
children.note: A £150 rebate paid to eligible low-income households over winter, recovered from suppliers and ultimately spread across all bill-payers.

children.label: Green Gas Levy
children.source: DESNZ Green Gas Support Scheme Regulations 2021 (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/green-gas-support-scheme-and-green-gas-levy). Funds biomethane injection into the gas grid.
children.note: Funds the Green Gas Support Scheme, which subsidises biomethane injection into the gas grid.

children.label: Other policy levies
children.source: Aggregate of smaller statutory levies and admin charges within the Ofgem cap's policy-cost component (capacity market admin, supplier-of-last-resort levies). Per-component breakdown not separately published; treated here as a residual.
children.note: Smaller scheme costs and administrative levies attached to the gas bill.

children.label: Supplier margin (Centrica plc)
children.source: Ofgem EBIT allowance ~1.9% of cap; Centrica plc Annual Report 2023
children.note: The profit allowance built into the price cap. Ofgem permits an EBIT margin of around 1.9% of the cap value. This is where the user's bill becomes the supplier's profit — and where it then flows out to shareholders, executives, the taxman and reinvestment.

children.label: Corporation tax & energy profits levy
children.source: Illustrative allocation of the supplier-margin slice. Centrica plc reports group-level totals for tax, dividends, capex, executive pay and retained earnings; the share specifically attributable to UK retail-supply margin is not separately disclosed. Numbers reflect directional weighting based on each company's stated capital allocation.
children.note: Profits from gas supply attract standard corporation tax (25% from April 2023). Centrica's upstream gas production is also subject to ring-fence corporation tax (30%) plus the Energy Profits Levy (35%). Click to follow these payments into the UK Income Tax tree.

children.label: Dividends to shareholders
children.source: Illustrative allocation of the supplier-margin slice. Centrica plc reports group-level totals for tax, dividends, capex, executive pay and retained earnings; the share specifically attributable to UK retail-supply margin is not separately disclosed. Numbers reflect directional weighting based on each company's stated capital allocation.
children.note: Centrica plc is listed on the FTSE 100 with around 5.4 billion shares in issue. The largest shareholders are typically institutional investors: BlackRock, Vanguard, Legal & General Investment Management. Through pension funds and ISAs many UK households are indirect Centrica shareholders. The 2023 full-year dividend was 4.0p per share.

children.label: Capital expenditure & reinvestment
children.source: Illustrative allocation of the supplier-margin slice. Centrica plc reports group-level totals for tax, dividends, capex, executive pay and retained earnings; the share specifically attributable to UK retail-supply margin is not separately disclosed. Numbers reflect directional weighting based on each company's stated capital allocation.
children.note: Funds new investment by the group: Centrica's 15% stake in Sizewell C nuclear, the reopening and expansion of the Rough gas-storage field, battery storage, and trading-business growth. Reinvested profit grows the asset base rather than being paid out.

children.label: Executive remuneration
children.source: Illustrative allocation of the supplier-margin slice. Centrica plc reports group-level totals for tax, dividends, capex, executive pay and retained earnings; the share specifically attributable to UK retail-supply margin is not separately disclosed. Numbers reflect directional weighting based on each company's stated capital allocation.
children.note: Centrica's CEO Chris O'Shea reported total remuneration of around £8.2m for FY2023, predominantly from share awards rather than salary. This figure covers the entire Centrica group, not British Gas alone, so only a fraction is attributable to retail-supply profits.

payRatio.label: Chris O'Shea, CEO — FY2023 single figure
payRatio.caveats: Single-figure remuneration is the standard UK reporting basis: salary, bonus, share awards and pension combined. Verify against Centrica's 2023 Annual Report Directors' Remuneration Report.

children.label: Retained for the business
children.source: Illustrative allocation of the supplier-margin slice. Centrica plc reports group-level totals for tax, dividends, capex, executive pay and retained earnings; the share specifically attributable to UK retail-supply margin is not separately disclosed. Numbers reflect directional weighting based on each company's stated capital allocation.
children.note: Earnings kept on the balance sheet to fund future operations, smooth volatility, and rebuild buffers depleted during the 2021-22 supplier collapses (Centrica was awarded the Bulb customer book under the Special Administration Regime).

children.label: Other allowances
children.source: Ofgem cap methodology — adjustment, headroom, smart-meter net cost
children.note: Smaller line items inside the cap: an adjustment allowance for unrecovered costs, a headroom allowance to absorb forecasting error, and the net cost of the smart-meter rollout.

children.label: Unallocated / cost recovery
children.source: Residual — reflects variation between cap components and actual bills
children.note: The cap is built from a model. Real bills include cost-recovery items (under- or over-collection from prior periods) and supplier-specific adjustments. Treated here as unallocated so the bill totals to 100%.

children.label: VAT
children.source: HMRC; reduced rate of 5% applies to domestic energy
children.note: Domestic energy is charged at the 5% reduced rate of VAT. Strictly this is 5% of the rest of the bill, not 5% of the total. Click to follow VAT receipts into the UK Income Tax tree.

root.label: A 330ml can of Coca-Cola — UK supermarket
root.source: PRICE — no single authoritative source. ONS CPI tracks soft drinks at category level (https://www.ons.gov.uk/economy/inflationandpriceindices) but not at SKU level, and Coca-Cola does not publish per-can recommended retail prices. The 85p default is a representative single-can supermarket price for 2025-26 based on observed Tesco / Sainsbury's shelf pricing; real prices range ~75p to £1.20 by retailer, location, and pack-size pro-rata. STRUCTURE — HMRC for VAT (Notice 701/40) and SDIL (Finance Act 2017 Part 2); CCEP investor relations (https://www.cocacolaep.com/investors) and TCCC 10-K filings (https://investors.coca-colacompany.com) for the corporate splits; supermarket-margin and CCEP cost-component sub-splits are industry-illustrative because exact contract terms across this supply chain are commercially confidential.
root.note: A standard 330ml can of Coke from a UK supermarket (representative price ~85p; actual prices range from about 75p to £1.20 depending on retailer, location and pack size). The chain of hands is longer than the price suggests: HMRC takes two bites (VAT and the sugar tax), the supermarket takes its retail margin, the bottler — Coca-Cola Europacific Partners — takes the largest share, and a famous concentrate fee flows from CCEP to The Coca-Cola Company in Atlanta. The headline figures are firm (VAT and SDIL are statutory); the deeper splits are illustrative.

children.label: VAT (20%)
children.source: HMRC VAT Notice 701/40 (food and drink) — https://www.gov.uk/guidance/food-products-and-vat-notice-70114. Soft drinks are standard-rated; the food-and-drink zero-rating does NOT apply.
children.note: Soft drinks are standard-rated, so VAT is one-sixth of the sticker price. On an 85p can the VAT is roughly 14p. Click to follow into the UK Income Tax tree.

children.label: Soft Drinks Industry Levy (sugar tax)
children.source: HMRC Soft Drinks Industry Levy — Finance Act 2017 Part 2 (https://www.gov.uk/guidance/soft-drinks-industry-levy). Higher band: 24p/litre for drinks ≥8g sugar/100ml; lower band: 18p/litre for 5–8g/100ml. Standard Coke at ~10.6g/100ml falls in the higher band.
children.note: Standard Coke is over the 8g sugar / 100ml threshold so attracts the higher SDIL rate of 24p per litre — about 8p on a 330ml can. The levy is paid by the bottler to HMRC and passed through in the wholesale price to the retailer. Introduced 2018; standard Coke chose not to reformulate. Click to follow into the UK Income Tax tree.

children.source: Industry estimates; branded soft-drink gross margin typically 10–20%
